title: Power of Play Study
official: The Power of Play: Evaluating an Imagination-Inspired Medical Garment for Children
summary:
This project will evaluate whether SuperTee, an imaginative hospital gown designed to help children embody empowering characters (e.g., superheroes), can reduce anxiety and improve coping skills among young children receiving hospital care.

Research Question 1: Is receiving the SuperTee garment associated with lower parent-reported levels of children's anxiety compared to baseline?

Research Question 2: Does receiving the SuperTee garment promote improvements in parent-reported levels of children's coping skills compared to baseline?

This study will also investigate the initial feasibility of SuperTee, as well as a potential mechanism through which it works (psychological distancing) .

Secondary Question 1: Do parent-reported levels of their child's ability to psychologically distance themselves from difficult situations explain differences in children's responses to the SuperTee intervention?

Secondary Question 2: Do parents and children like the SuperTee medical garment and find it to be practical and easy to use? How often do the children use it?
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* The study participants will be children, aged 4-7 years, undergoing medical treatment at the Fairview Masonic Children's Hospital in Minneapolis, MN for chronic health conditions.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Children who do not speak English, have an intellectual disability, have uncorrected vision or hearing disabilities, are terminally ill or do not have access to a smartphone, tablet, or computer that is able to run online surveys will be excluded from the final study sample.
